//: The variants pack: weapon SIDEGRADES as DATA (docs/VARIANTS.md §1 and §7,
docs/PACKS.md kind 7). A variant is a named override set applied to ONE
base weapon — never a new id, never new behaviour, never a feel field.
shared/src/variants.ts is the only thing that decides whether a line here
is allowed to exist: the whitelist and its bands, the ±12% power budget,
and the strict-dominance refusal that forbids a straight upgrade.
WHY EXACTLY TWO, AND WHY THESE TWO.
A variant has ONE base, so a pack that wants to prove the machine end to
end needs one entry per archetype the machine treats differently. There
are two that matter here: HITSCAN, where pellets, headshots and falloff
are all live, and PROJECTILE, where falloff* is inert (a projectile
stores its damage at spawn) and projectileSpeed is the handling axis.
Slug Shotgun is the hitscan half and carries a pellet change AND a rate
change in one row, so a single entry exercises the payload band
(damage × pellets) as well as the budget. Swift Rocket is the projectile
half. A THIRD entry would exist only to make the table look fuller, and
an entry nobody can justify is content that has to be balanced, migrated
and dormanted forever — see the removal note below.
SLUG SHOTGUN. One 62-damage slug instead of seven 11-damage pellets: the
per-shot payload goes 77 -> 62 (inside 0.25..2.5× of the base) while the
cone tightens 0.09 -> 0.012 rad and the useful range stretches 28 -> 44 m.
It PAYS in rate of fire, 75 -> 42 rpm. Budget 1.0196, +2.0%: dps ×0.528,
range ×1.503, handling ×2.013. Better at reach and worse at throughput,
which is what a sidegrade is.
SWIFT ROCKET. A rocket that travels 46 -> 66 m/s and fires 88 -> 104 rpm,
paying with a 92 -> 82 direct hit and a 4.4 -> 3.8 m blast. Budget 0.9879,
-1.2%: dps ×0.978, splash ×0.864, handling ×1.145. Note what is NOT here:
falloffStart/End/Min/Curve are INERT on a projectile and the parser
refuses them outright rather than pricing them at zero, and spread* has a
band of 0..0 against a base cone of exactly 0 — so speed, rate, damage and
splash are the whole of the projectile's vocabulary.
REMOVING an id from this file is the destructive direction, exactly as it
is for items: every owned copy goes dormant and its holder falls back to
the BASE weapon at the next read, so they keep firing — just not the gun
they earned. The gate counts them (variants.dormanted). A re-cut pack is a
NEW version directory under DOOMCRAFT_PACKS, never an in-place edit of
this file: this file IS variants@1 on a host with no packs root.
